questions.question: What is the central irony in the poem regarding the “polished traﬃc”?
options: It rushes past admiring the countryside.
It stops to buy goods from the roadside stand.
It symbolizes modern progress that ignores rural suﬀering.
It brings prosperity to rural areas.
questions.explanation: It symbolizes modern progress that ignores rural suﬀering.

questions.question: The poet’s tone in “The hurt to the scenery wouldn’t be my complaint” is best described as:
What does the poet imply by "you have the money, but if you want to be mean, why keep your money"?
options: The roadside vendors charge too much.
The drivers are rich but unwilling to help.
The countryside is full of greedy people.
questions.explanation: The drivers are rich but unwilling to help.

questions.question: The signs with “N turned wrong and S turned wrong” symbolise:
options: Poor education and innocence of villagers
The reversed direction of modern society
questions.explanation: Poor education and innocence of villagers

questions.question: The phrase "beneﬁcent beasts of prey" is an example of:
What is the underlying emotion in “the trusting sorrow of what is unsaid”?
What do the "greedy good-doers" ironically refer to?
options: City people who exploit rural areas while claiming to help
questions.explanation: City people who exploit rural areas while claiming to help

questions.question: The poet mentions “sleep all day” and “destroy their sleeping at night” to suggest:
What does the speaker’s reluctant empathy for the rural poor suggest?
options: He wants to escape from rural areas
He is torn between pity and helplessness
questions.explanation: He is torn between pity and helplessness

questions.question: The phrase “childish longing in vain” most likely refers to:
options: Unrealistic rural dreams for city luxuries

questions.explanation: Unrealistic rural dreams for city luxuries
